Long, long ago, in the hot and sunny land of Egypt, there lived a people who dreamed of being free. And soon, a very special boy would be born among them.
To keep her baby safe, his mother placed him in a little basket and set it on the river. The basket drifted quietly among the reeds.
Pharaoh's daughter found the little basket by the river. She named the baby Moses and raised him as her very own son.
Moses grew up in a palace. But one day he saw how unfairly his people were being treated, and he went away, far into the desert.
In the desert, Moses became a shepherd. The days passed quietly — sheep, sunshine, and long walks among the stones.
One day, Moses saw a bush that was on fire — but it didn't burn up. A voice came from the flames: "Go and lead My people out of Egypt."
Moses went to Pharaoh and said: "Let my people go." But Pharaoh refused to listen.
Then trouble after trouble came upon Egypt. Again and again Moses went to Pharaoh, but Pharaoh was stubborn.
At last, the Pharaoh let the people go. That night, they gathered together and followed Moses out of Egypt.
But Pharaoh changed his mind and sent his army in chariots racing after them. The people were terrified — the sea was ahead, and the soldiers were closing in from behind.
Moses raised his staff over the water. And a miracle happened: the sea parted, revealing a dry path through the middle.
The people walked along the bottom of the sea as if it were a road. On their left and right, walls of water stood tall.
When everyone had crossed, the water rushed back. The people were safe at last, and they celebrated with joy, thankful for their freedom.
In the desert, the people grew tired and hungry. Then bread called manna fell from the sky, and clean water flowed right out of a rock.
Moses climbed up Mount Sinai. There, among the clouds, he heard the words that God wanted to give to the people.
Moses came down from the mountain carrying two stone tablets. Written on them were the most important rules for living a good life — rules for all the people.
And the people journeyed on — through the desert toward the promised land, carrying the good rules in their hearts. A new road lay ahead, and hope walked with them.
